chunks: It is narrated from Al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:

“My father عليه السلام purchased a land called al-ʿUrayḍ. When he made it binding, he stood up and went away. So I said to him, ‘O my father, you hastened to stand up.’ He said, ‘O my son, I wanted the sale to become binding.’”

key_terms.أَرْضًا: a piece of land; the property being sold
key_terms.اسْتَوْجَبَهَا: made it binding/confirmed it; finalized the transaction
key_terms.اشْتَرَى: purchased; entered into a sale transaction
key_terms.الْعُرَيْضُ: al-ʿUrayḍ; the name of the land mentioned in the report
key_terms.الْقِيَامِ: standing up; rising from the session of sale
key_terms.يَجِبَ الْبَيْعُ: the sale becomes binding; the transaction becomes legally concluded

ai.seo_question: How does physical separation affect the binding nature of a sale in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام, after purchasing land, promptly departed so that the sale would become binding. It indicates a legal significance to separation after a transaction and is cited in the context of fiqh discussions on the conclusion of a sale contract.
